Content: The excerpt below is from the `1919` Treaty of Versailles.

:box:`ultext(Article 232)`

The Allied and Associated Governments, however, require, and Germany undertakes, that she will make compensation for all damage done to the civilian population of the Allied and Associated Powers and to their property during the period of the belligerency of each as an Allied or Associated Power against Germany by such aggression by land, by sea and from the air. . . . . . . Germany undertakes, in addition to the compensation for damage elsewhere . . . , to make reimbursement of all sums which Belgium has borrowed from the Allied and Associated Governments up to `text(November 11, 1918)`, together with interest at the rate of `text(five per cent)`.

	Source: Library of Congress/Public Domain

A.Choice: It would weaken German economic recovery.

B.Choice: German property was also damaged by enemy action.

C.Choice: It would give European allied nations excessive power.

D.Choice: European allied nations were also responsible for wartime damage.

Content: The excerpt below is from a diplomatic note sent by U.S. Secretary of State John Hay in `1899`.

:box:The Government of the United States would be pleased to see His German Majesty’s Government give formal assurances, and lend its cooperation in securing like assurances from the other interested powers, that each, within its respective sphere of whatever influence —
	`text(First)`. Will in no way interfere with any treaty port or any vested interest within any so-called “sphere of interest” or leased territory it may have in China.
	`text(Second)`. That the Chinese treaty tariff of the time being shall apply to all merchandise landed or shipped to all such ports as are within said “sphere of interest” . . . , no matter to what nationality it may belong, and that duties so leviable shall be collected by the Chinese Government.
	`text(Third)`. That it will levy no higher harbor dues on vessels of another nationality frequenting any port in such “sphere” than shall be levied on vessels of its own nationality.

	Source: Library of Congress/Public Domain
Why did the U.S. government pursue this foreign policy with the leading world powers in `1899`?

A.Choice: The United States wanted to deter military conflicts between European powers in China.

B.Choice: The United States hoped to prevent territorial expansion by Japanese forces in China.

C.Choice: The United States hoped to secure equal economic opportunities in China.

D.Choice: The United States wanted to build new naval bases in China.
